Header: Plutella xylostella English: cabbage moth; European honeysuckle leafroller

Prevention: Rotate cabbage, rape, broccoli or cauliflower with any of the following crops: tomato, onion, maize, or sweet potato
Plant early in the season to avoid the period of diamond back moth build-up
Remove and bury/burn crop debris including weeds at least 4 weeks prior to sowing to reduce
Plant seedling beds away from production fields
Transplant only healthy seedlings free of eggs, caterpillars and pupae of the
Intercrop with tomato, chilies, marigolds or mustard.
Mustard acts as a trap crop for adult moths.
Plant two rows of mustard for every 25 of cabbage
Slash left-over cabbage stems after harvest to avoid regrowth which can act as a diamond back moth breeding area
After harvest, plough the field to expose any pests harbouring in the soil
Monitoring: Crucifer family (rape, broccoli, cauliflower, chinese cabbage)
Inspect crop weekly, especially the underside of leaves
Look for small, grey moths, which have a diamond pattern on their wings when at rest
Look for caterpillars which are yellowish green to green and around 1 cm long when fully grown.
They hang from a web when disturbed and tend to appear at the four leaf stage of cabbage growth
Look for damage on leaves: irregular holes, windowing and skeletonised underside
DBM adults using pheromone traps, placing 2-4 traps/Ha.
Check traps twice a week early in the morning.
Use control when 5 + adult moths are caught in a trap
Alternatively, you may consider direct control when you notice 2 to 3 young larvae per plant
Direct Control: Uproot and bury or burn cabbage debris, if burning is permitted in your country
Crush larvae by hand if noticed when numbers are few
Apply aqueous solution of botanical pesticide neem or tephrosia (40g/L soak over night and seive)
Alternatively spray chilli mixed with water and few chopped pieces of bar soap or drops of liquid soap
Plant trap crops such as mustard and rape at the edges of the the field to reduce
See if these biological controls are available in your country
Use overhead irrigation which dislodges the pest from the plant surface
